title: hotfix/slo-enforcer-backoff-regional-hysteresis-fix
author: Samira Gupta
description: Motivation: During a recent regional incident we observed the SLO enforcer's backoff+regional-failover path thrashing under rapid partial-region failures which caused aggressive double-load-shedding and subsequent downstream cascading failovers. This PR fixes a race in the backoff ordering and adds hysteresis to the regional failover path so we do not immediately escalate multiple failovers in quick succession. Summary of changes: adjust backoff priority queue ordering (favor older backoffs with an adjusted penalty), introduce a hysteresis timer to the regional-failover coordinator, add defensive checks when applying global load-shed decisions to avoid duplicate shedding for same request sources, add unit and e2e tests that reproduce the thrashing scenario, and add metrics and dashboard tiles for backoff_count, hysteresis_active, and regional_failover_rate. Rollout: canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with SRE monitoring. Checklist: [x] Reproduced failure locally with test harness; [x] Added unit tests; [x] Added e2e reproduction test; [x] Added observability changes and dashboards; [x] Ran load tests that show stable SLOs across simulated partial-region failures. Risk: medium; changes target the enforcer ordering logic and failover coordination; comprehensive tests and staged rollout recommended. Rollback plan: revert to previous image and disable failover coordinator by feature flag if we see regression. Related: ENG-8421, incident-2026-02-14.

review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Can you explain why we prefer older backoffs over higher penalty? Author: The root cause was starvation of older requests leading to repeated re-evaluation and duplicate failovers; tie-breaker avoids reordering during concurrent updates.
Lina Park: Add an integration test that simulates two regions flapping quickly. Author: Added tests/e2e/partial_region_thrash.yaml that reproduces the scenario and validated in CI.

Marco Ruiz: Can we gate the new hysteresis with a feature flag to allow quick rollback? Author: Yes - config flag slo_enforcer.enable_hysteresis added; rollout plan uses flag to enable on canary first.
ci_checks: e2e: pass (reran once due to flake)
release_notes: Hotfix: fix race in SLO enforcer backoff ordering and add hysteresis to regional failover to prevent thrashing under partial-region failures. Improves stability of SLO enforcement and reduces cascading failovers. Rollout via feature flag and staged canary.
deployment_notes: Canary image pushed to registry: redwood/slo-enforcer:hotfix-618273. Enable slo_enforcer.enable_hysteresis=false by default; flip to true on canary cluster and verify metrics for 30m, then proceed 5%->25%->100%. If regressions observed revert image and disable flag.
observability_changes: Added metrics: slo_enforcer.backoff_count, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_active, slo_enforcer.regional_failover_rate. Dashboard: SLO Enforcer -> Backoff & Failover tile added. Alert: FailoverRate > 0.1 for 5m -> Pager.
